thread:
maya: Hey team — first week here. Trying to get the local stack running with `docker-compose up` from the repo root and I'm hitting two things: Postgres keeps restarting with errors about `pg_hba.conf` / server config, and the redis container exits saying it can't open `/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf`. Any quick pointers?

sam: Welcome! Did you run the setup script in the README? `scripts/setup-dev.sh` sets up the dev volume dirs and .env.

maya: I ran it but might have missed a step. Here's the minimal override I added (docker-compose.override.yml):

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./dev/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  redis:
    image: redis:7
    command: redis-server /usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf
    volumes:
      - ./dev/redis/redis.conf:/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf
```

jon: Two things jump out: the postgres volume mount can inherit root ownership on mac/linux depending on how it was created, and for redis you're forcing a config file that might not exist. For Postgres either remove `./dev/postgres` so the container can init it, or set ownership to the postgres UID (`chown -R 999:999 dev/postgres`).

laura: For redis, if you don't actually have a custom config, drop the `command:` line — redis will start with defaults. We keep a canonical config at `infra/local/redis.conf` in the repo; easiest fix is `ln -s infra/local/redis.conf dev/redis/redis.conf` or change the volume to mount that file.

maya: I'm on mac. I checked `dev/postgres` and it's owned by root. I did `sudo chown -R 999:999 dev/postgres` and restarted, but Postgres then started to initialize and later crashed with `FATAL: permission denied for directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_tblspc"`.

sam: Stop containers, `rm -rf dev/postgres/*` (only if you don't have anything to keep), then `docker-compose up` so Postgres can create files as the container user. If permissions keep acting up it's usually Docker Desktop file sharing or a sticky mount bug on macOS.

infra-bot: @maya FYI there's a known Docker Desktop mount permission issue on certain macOS versions — see infra KB: https://intra.redwood/infra/kb/docker-mounts. If it continues, open an infra ticket and include your Docker Desktop version.

maya: Removing the files fixed Postgres, thanks. For redis I changed the volume to `infra/local/redis.conf` like laura suggested and it now starts. Two quick follow-ups: 1) How do I run DB migrations locally? 2) Any quick tips to speed up dev stack startup?

jon: Migrations: `./scripts/run-migrations.sh` will run them against the local DB. Or you can run `PGHOST=localhost PGUSER=rw psql -f migrations/001_init.sql` if you want manual control. To speed up startup, avoid mounting huge host folders (node_modules), use `:cached` on mac mounts (`./web:/app:cached`), set `COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT=3`, and use the `REDWOOD_DEV_MINIMAL=true` env to skip heavy services.

laura: Also use `make dev START=web,api` to only start minimal services for iterative work. We have a `make dev-full` for full stack but it's slower.

maya: Perfect — that gets me moving. Tagging infra/ops for visibility: @infra-bot @ops-bot :rocket:

ops-bot: Noted. If multiple devs hit mac mount permission issues we'll provision a tiny Linux VM image for local development.

sam: If you want a live walkthrough, join onboarding office hours tomorrow at 11am — we'll step through the local stack and common fixes.

maya: Will do, thanks everyone!
